title: Trivial Field Comment Noise
pattern: Doc-comment on a struct field that merely translates the field's snake_case name into standard English words.
why_bad: Adds noise and maintenance weight. Developers learn to skip over doc-comments entirely when they are filled with obvious text, risking missing actual non-obvious details.
detection: Field doc-comments where the text matches the field name characters, ignoring case and spacing.
counterexample: A field doc-comment carrying actual invariants, e.g. '/// The day of the month (1-31, adjusted for leap years).'
fix: Delete the comment if the field name is self-explanatory, or expand it with actual business invariants (e.g., valid bounds).
source: Robert C. Martin, *Clean Code* (2008), Chapter 4 ("Noise Comments"); John K. Ousterhout, *A Philosophy of Software Design* (2018), Chapter 13.2.
